sentences.text: The appellants filed this intra-Court appeal challenging the order dated 16.09.2021, passed in W.P.No.43815/2011.

2. Brief facts leading rise to filing of this appeal are as under:
- 10 - Respondent No.1 filed a writ petition challenging the preliminary notification dated 30.03.1989, and final notification dated 07.10.1999, issued by the State Government for the purpose of acquisition for formation of 'Banashankari V Stage Layout' or in the alternative to direct the State Government to de-notify the scheduled lands measuring 3 acres 16 guntas in Sy.No.50 and 2 acres 27 guntas in Sy.No.53 of Uttarahalli Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.
The learned Single Judge after hearing the parties, dismissed the writ petition vide order dated 16.09.2021.

The appellants aggrieved by the order of dismissal, filed this writ appeal on the ground that respondent No.1 entered into an agreement to sell dated 07.07.2005 and 21.08.2007, with Dandapani N. K. and others for sale of aforesaid lands.

Subsequently, entire consideration amount was paid by Late Dandapani and others and respondent No.1 executed registered sale deed on 29.08.2007, pending for consideration of registration in the office of the Sub- Registrar, Banashankari.

It is submitted that respondent - 11 - No.1 had not disclosed about the acquisition of land by the State Government and executed sale deed in favour of the appellants and without arraying the appellants as parties in the said writ petition, respondent No.1 has filed the writ petition challenging the acquisition proceedings.
Hence, the appellants filed an application seeking leave of the Court to file the present writ appeal.
3. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent No.3 on I.A.No.3/2022.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants have purchased the lands under registered sale deed in the year 2007 and respondent No.1 without disclosing about the acquisition of lands, executed agreement of sale and also registered sale deed.
He submits that respondent No.1 without arraying the appellants as parties in the writ petition, has filed the writ petition.
The learned Single Judge dismissed the writ petition.
He submits that the appellants are being - 12 - deprived of their legitimate right in the lands purchased by him.
He submits that the learned Single Judge has committed an error in passing the impugned order.
Hence prayed to grant leave to prefer the writ appeal.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Additional Government Advocate supports the impugned order.

6. Perused the records and considered the submission of the learned counsel for the parties.
7.

It is not in dispute that the State Government has issued preliminary notification dated 30.03.1989 and final notification dated 07.10.1999 for the purpose of acquisition for formation of 'Banashankari V Stage Layout'.
After initiating acquisition proceedings, respondent No.1 executed registered sale deed in favour of the appellants.
Respondent No.1 challenged the preliminary notification and final notification.
After initiating acquisition proceedings, respondent No.1 sold the aforesaid lands in favour of the appellants, the subsequent purchasers of the - 13 - property.
After issuance of notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the subsequent purchasers cannot challenge the acquisition proceedings.
At the most, the purchasers would be entitled to claim compensation by virtue of sale made in their favour.

The said view is being supported by the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of UNION OF INDIA VS.
SHIVKUMAR BHARGAVA & ORS., reported in AIR 1995 SC 812.

The said view is subsequently being reiterated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of SHIV KUMAR VS. UNION OF INDIA reported in AIR 2019 SC 5374 and GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI VS. SUNIL JAIN & ORS., reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 36.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI VS. SUNIL JAIN & ORS., reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 36
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the appellants are the purchasers subsequent to issuance of initiation of acquisition proceedings.
Hence, the appellants have no right to challenge the impugned order as the appellants do not fall within the definition of the word 'owner'.
Hence, in view of the above discussion, we do not find any grounds to grant - 14 - leave to the appellants to file the writ appeal.
Accordingly, we decline to entertain the application filed by the appellants in I.A.No.3/2022 seeking for grant of leave for filing the present writ appeal.
Accordingly, I.A.No.3/2022 is dismissed.
9. Consequently, the appeal is dismissed.

In view of disposal of the writ appeal, pending IAs., if any,
do not survive for consideration and are accordingly disposed of.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The appellants aggrieved by the order of dismissal, filed this writ appeal on the ground that respondent No.1 entered into an agreement to sell dated 07.07.2005 and 21.08.2007, with Dandapani N. K. and others for sale of aforesaid lands.
After initiating acquisition proceedings, respondent No.1 executed registered sale deed in favour of the appellants.
Respondent No.1 challenged the preliminary notification and final notification.
After initiating acquisition proceedings, respondent No.1 sold the aforesaid lands in favour of the appellants, the subsequent purchasers of the - 13 - property.
After issuance of notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the subsequent purchasers cannot challenge the acquisition proceedings.
At the most, the purchasers would be entitled to claim compensation by virtue of sale made in their favour.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants have purchased the lands under registered sale deed in the year 2007 and respondent No.1 without disclosing about the acquisition of lands, executed agreement of sale and also registered sale deed.
He submits that the appellants are being - 12 - deprived of their legitimate right in the lands purchased by him.
He submits that the learned Single Judge has committed an error in passing the impugned order.
